algorithm.title: Scleritis or Episcleritis, Suspected: Evaluation and Treatment.

cell.label: Red eye. Examine eye and ocular adnexa.
Redness; no pain or foreign body sensation only; blanches with phenylephrine 10%?
Trial of no treatment or artificial tears 4 times per day and prn.
Fluorometholone 0.1% 1 drop 4 times per day for 1 wk, followed by taper over 2 wk. (Okay to substitute other steroid such as loteprednol or prednisolone acetate.)
Violet hue more than redness; scleral edema; tenderness; vision change; failure to blanch with phenylephrine 10%?
Complete ophthalmic examination and systemic evaluation. Treat underlying disease if any.
Topical prednisolone acetate 1% every 1-2 h or oral NSAID (indomethacin or ibuprofen or other).
Systemic steroid (prednisone 1 mg/kg/d) versus peribulbar steroid injection.
Systemic immunosuppression (methotrexate, cyclosporine, cyclophosphamide, azathioprine, TNF inhibitors).
